verdict.summary: The video streaming app's recommendation AI may be non-compliant with Indian data protection laws due to the lack of explicit user consent for collecting and storing watch history data locally on users' devices.

issues.title: Lack of Explicit User Consent
issues.description: User watch history is collected without explicit consent, which may conflict with Indian data protection laws such as The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019.
issues.remediation: Implement opt-in mechanism for users to consent to the collection and storage of watch history data

issues.title: Unclear Compliance with Indian Data Protection Laws
issues.description: The AI model's autonomous decision-making without human oversight raises concerns about potential non-compliance with Indian data protection laws.
issues.impact: Potential legal disputes or penalties in India
issues.remediation: Implement policies and procedures for data protection and user consent in compliance with Indian laws

evidence_cited.content: All bodies corporate are required to be in possession of reasonable security practices and procedures for the protection of sensitive personal data or information.
frameworks: The Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011

evidence_cited.content: Personal data must be processed in a fair and lawful manner with the consent of the data principal...
